_why: A stage that has produced no new progress line for this long is treated as stalled: the watcher (on the operator's machine) and the manifest (on the pod, independently) both pull the logs, terminate the instance, and stop.
20 minutes is the default because a stage that is working prints a line per run, and the shortest run in the campaign is minutes.

The per-stage overrides exist for the stages whose INDIVIDUAL runs are long enough that the runner legitimately prints nothing between run boundaries. They are sized to the longest single run, not to the whole stage: the stage's own declared wall-clock timeout (STAGE_TIMEOUTS in scripts/mlsys_manifest.sh) remains the hard backstop, so a wrong value here cannot cost more than a stage's budget.
Both sides read THIS file, so the two watchdogs cannot drift apart. A per-stage value must be justified; an override with no reason is how a watchdog quietly stops watching.

WARNING (2026-10-08T18:29Z): every per-stage value here is sized to the longest SINGLE RUN, but the progress signal is only written BETWEEN STAGES. Any stage whose total wall time exceeds its value will be killed by the watchdog while it is working. engine_cap_smoke was raised for that reason; the others (natural_f1_128k 90 vs 6.5h, natural_spec_gated_256k 180 vs 13.0h, correction_note_evidence 40 vs 2.1h) need the same review.

Measured on the first two rows of this run (ctx 131072, all four rows at that context): cap=64 spec 122.7s, cap=64 target-only 245.7s, i.e. 1.92 and 3.84 s/token. The stage runs the 7 candidates in configs/mlsys_rope_candidates.json at 131072, 4x262144 and 2x524288, i.e. 2228224 context-tokens = 3.48x the calibration run that JUST MEASURED 753s for 9 candidates over 640000 context-tokens on this same pod. Two bounds follow from that measurement, and neither exceeds the 2.0h projection: a pure per-candidate (fixed) cost gives 753*7/9 = 586s = 9.8 min, and a pure context-proportional cost gives 753*3.48 = 2621s = 43.7 min. The truth is between those, because each candidate pays a fixed 1024-token perplexity and 200-token generation on top of its prefill. So the measured analogue is 10-44 min against a 120-minute projection: the projection is conservative and 240 min is ~5.5x the upper bound.

_todo_after_campaign: Do NOT implement mid-campaign (recorded 2026-10-08T18:45Z, on instruction).

The root fix is for both watchdogs to poll ~/manifest.log for per-row progress instead of results/mlsys/RUN_LOG.txt. That log carries the runner's [n/N] and per-row lines, so a stage that is working would show progress continuously and the threshold could go back to a per-run value sized as the file's _why originally intended.
Until then every value in this file is a whole-stage budget and must be reviewed whenever a stage's estimate changes.
_liveness_why: The byte-level liveness rule: how long ~/manifest.log may go WITHOUT GROWING (in bytes, not in lines) while a stage is running, before the pod watchdog and the operator's watcher both treat it as a stall, pull, terminate and stop. It is stricter than every per-stage value above on purpose, and it is NOT overridable per stage: a per-stage override would let exactly the stage that hangs opt out of the check that exists to catch it. MEASURED BEFORE CHOSEN (2026-10-09): the longest legitimate silence anywhere in the campaign's manifest logs is a 1M-token target prefill at 6.29 min, measured as ttft across 146 rows (the prefill is silent: the runner's first line for a phase is printed when the phase is DONE). 15 min is 2.4x that, and it is below the 2x bound the operator set, so the bound does not bind. Realistic 8x prefills are far shorter -- 256k, the longest context in the approved stages, is roughly a quarter of that. WHY IT WAS ADDED: the per-stage values only cover a stage that produces no RUN_LOG line, so a hang INSIDE a stage is invisible to them. On 2026-10-09T00:00Z the teacher-forced probe deadlocked: rank 0 entered a ring collective alone, wrote nothing for 62.0 min, and was only stopped by the NCCL watchdog at 3600 s. engine_cap_smoke's own threshold is 240 min, so nothing fired -- 8xA100-80GB billed for 62 min (~$43) on a run that could never finish. The same logs contain that 62.0 min deadlock and a 66.3 min one from the earlier failed run, both visible as gaps with no output at all, which is exactly what this rule catches.
